research_question: In children with otitis media with effusion (OME), does intranasal corticosteroid treatment (e.g. mometasone, beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone), given alone or added to a co-treatment that both arms receive equally, reduce the persistence of middle ear effusion at the first assessment up to 1 month (≤6 weeks) after starting treatment, compared with no steroid treatment (no treatment or the same co-treatment alone)?
treatment_label: Intranasal corticosteroid spray (± co-treatment given equally to both arms)
control_label: No steroid treatment (no treatment, watchful waiting, or the same co-treatment alone)
outcome_description: Number of children (or ears, if reported per ear with both ears combined) with persistent middle ear effusion at the first assessment up to 1 month (≤6 weeks) after starting treatment, extracted as event counts and totals per arm. Persistence = effusion still present at follow-up: type B tympanogram (or type C2 / non-type-A if that is how the study defines treatment failure), "not cured", "no improvement", or "persistent effusion" on otoscopy/otomicroscopy. Resolution/cure = type A tympanogram or complete clearance of effusion. If a study reports resolution, cure, or improvement, convert to persistence as total minus resolved. If the headline result is a multi-category or ordinal scale (complete remission / partial remission / no change / exacerbation), derive persistence counts from the post-treatment tympanogram-type or cure/no-cure table per arm rather than discarding the study. For trials with more than two arms, use only the intranasal-steroid arm and the no-steroid arm receiving the same co-treatment; ignore oral-steroid, montelukast, antihistamine-only and other active arms.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR < 1) means fewer children/ears with persistent middle ear effusion in the intranasal steroid arm than in the no-steroid arm — i.e. the result favours intranasal steroids (more resolution of OME) at up to 1 month.

inclusion_criteria: Studies of children (or predominantly paediatric samples) with otitis media with effusion / glue ear / secretory otitis media
Includes an intranasal (nasal spray or nasal drop) corticosteroid arm compared with an arm not receiving intranasal steroid (no treatment, watchful waiting, or the same co-treatment alone)
Reports some quantitative outcome on effusion status (e.g. tympanogram type, cure/resolution/persistence counts, or data from which persistence counts can be derived) at or before about 6 weeks
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, case report, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between an intranasal steroid condition and a no-steroid control condition (single-arm or before-after only), or the control arm received a placebo nasal spray, or the steroid was oral/systemic/intratympanic rather than intranasal
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts per arm, proportions, means+SDs, or test statistics convertible to a risk ratio)

Completely unrelated to otitis media with effusion in children, or reports only excluded outcomes (hearing thresholds/air-bone gap, symptom or parent-reported improvement, quality of life, adverse events) or only outcomes measured after 6 weeks
moderators_to_extract: Specific intranasal corticosteroid agent and dose
Co-treatment given equally to both arms (e.g. antibiotic, none)
Type of control (no treatment/watchful waiting vs co-treatment alone)
Definition of persistence (tympanogram type B only vs non-type-A vs otoscopic/clinical 'not cured')
Treatment duration and exact timing of first assessment (weeks)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias / randomisation and blinding status
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio (RR) with a random-effects model (DerSimonian–Laird or REML), using event counts (persistent effusion) and totals per arm. RR < 1 favours intranasal steroids. Where results are reported per ear, sum right and left ear events and totals; never use a single ear. Where resolution/cure is reported, derive persistence as total minus resolved. Apply a continuity correction only where a zero cell prevents estimation, and consider Peto OR or Mantel–Haenszel without correction in sensitivity analysis. Only the first assessment ≤6 weeks after treatment start is used from each trial.
single_outcome_target: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 1 month
